Rugged tablet for Micad FM (Micad estates and facilities software)

Micad FM is the helpdesk and maintenance module of Micad's estates and facilities software, made by Micad Systems (UK) Limited of Altrincham. Micad says its software is used by more than 180 of approximately 240 NHS trusts, and its case studies name Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, South London and Maudsley NHS Trust, Brunel University and the universities of Bristol and Bath. Since K1 Investment Management combined Micad with SINGU in July 2025, Micad has marketed its current CAFM platform as SINGU FM, but the Micad FM mobile app remains on Google Play and the App Store.

Micad describes the app as used by maintenance operatives for the Micad FM Helpdesk system. On site they work through a customisable jobs list, time jobs with a stopwatch, pause them or send them back to a supervisor, record stock parts, upload photos, raise remedial works against assets and capture signatures. The app uses one PDA licence from the customer's Micad FM system, needs Location Services on to send GPS data, and can create jobs and upload images while out of signal, synchronising when a connection returns. That is a day of corridors, plant rooms, roof spaces and van cabs, where a consumer tablet with a glass back and no ingress rating is at a disadvantage.

This page sets out what Micad publishes about the app's device requirements, which of the three Tuga rugged devices meet them, where Micad has published nothing (barcode scanning, NFC, screen size), and how to get a unit running. Tuga Hardware is independent of Micad, so everything about the software below is taken from Micad's own site, its Google Play and App Store listings and its G-Cloud listing.

Requirements

What Micad FM needs from a device

Each item below comes from Micad Systems (UK) Limited's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 5.0 or later

    The Micad FM app on Google Play (package uk.co.micad.fm, developer Micad Systems (UK)) requires Android 5.0 and up. The listing shows version 1.0.11, updated on 23 October 2024, with the release note 'Bug fixes and Android 14 support'. The Tuga A10 and A6 both run Android 14, so they meet the published requirement. Source: play.google.com

  • One PDA licence per handheld

    The listing states 'This App uses one PDA licence from the Micad FM system'. Each device you put in a technician's hands therefore needs a licence under your organisation's Micad contract. The app itself is free to download. Source: play.google.com

  • GPS and push notifications

    Micad states that 'Location Services' must be turned on to send GPS data and 'Notifications' must be turned on to receive push notifications. A device therefore needs a satellite positioning receiver and a data connection for notifications to arrive in the field. Source: play.google.com

  • Limited offline working

    Micad says the app's offline capabilities allow users to upload images and create jobs, which synchronise with the main Micad FM system when a connection is re-established. The listing does not say the full jobs list or job completion works without signal, and a public review dated 7 March 2024 reports not being able to upload job information or view the next job when out of signal. Plan for mobile data (4G or 5G) rather than relying on offline mode. Source: play.google.com

  • Camera for photos and a touchscreen for signatures

    The app's published feature list includes photo upload and signature capture on completion of a reactive task. A camera and a touchscreen that works with a finger or stylus are therefore needed. Micad does not publish a camera resolution or screen size. Source: play.google.com

  • Web platform: modern browser and an internet connection

    Micad's G-Cloud 14 listing for its Estates and Facilities Management SaaS Platform says the platform supports Microsoft Edge, Chrome and Safari and needs 'A valid internet connection to access Micad software'. No other hardware requirements are published. Windows users work in a browser. Source: applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk

  • No Windows version of the Micad FM app

    A search of the Microsoft Store for Micad returns only Micad Audit, published by Micad Systems (UK). Micad FM is not listed there, and Micad publishes the Micad FM app on Google Play and the App Store only, so a Windows device can only reach the Micad FM system through the browser-based platform. Source: apps.microsoft.com

  • Barcode, NFC and RFID: nothing published

    Neither the Google Play nor the App Store listing for Micad FM mentions barcode or QR scanning, NFC or RFID. Micad publishes a separate Micad GLN Scanner app for GS1 GLN location barcodes, but its listing says it 'Uses Micad IPR API' and needs a Micad IPR system, not Micad FM. Do not buy hardware for Micad FM on the assumption that scanning or tag reading is part of the app. Source: play.google.com

Worth knowing. Micad publishes no barcode, QR, NFC or RFID feature for the Micad FM app, so none of these devices should be bought for Micad FM on the expectation of scanning or tag reading. The A10 and A6 have NFC hardware and cameras, but any camera scanning is app-dependent and neither has a dedicated scan engine. The W10 cannot run the Micad FM mobile app, which Micad publishes for Android and iOS only; it suits browser-based use of the main platform. Buyers should also note that the Android app was last updated on 23 October 2024, carries a 2.0 star rating from 6 reviews on Google Play, and that reviews report freezing, being logged off and problems out of signal. Offline support is limited to creating jobs and uploading images, so a 4G or 5G SIM is advisable. Micad now markets its current CAFM platform as SINGU FM, so check with Micad that Micad FM remains the app your contract supports before ordering a fleet.
Setting up

Getting Micad FM running

  1. Confirm with your Micad account team or helpdesk administrator that a PDA licence from your Micad FM system is available for each device, since the app uses one PDA licence per handheld.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, sign in to a Google account (a managed work account if your organisation uses one) and install Micad FM from Google Play, developer Micad Systems (UK), package uk.co.micad.fm.
  3. Open the app and sign in with the credentials your Micad administrator issues. Allow Location Services and Notifications when prompted, as Micad states both must be on for GPS data and push notifications.
  4. Insert a 4G SIM (A10) or 5G SIM (A6) so that jobs and notifications reach the technician away from Wi-Fi, and note from the Micad FM listing that jobs and images created offline synchronise once a connection returns.
  5. For a W10 used by helpdesk or workshop staff, open the Micad web platform in Microsoft Edge or Chrome, sign in, and connect Ethernet or Wi-Fi for the required internet connection.
  6. Fit the hand strap (supplied with the A10) or belt holster (A6), and add a vehicle mounting dock or charging dock where the device lives in a van or returns to a workshop at the end of each shift.
